scope: Exact nonparametric ATE identification status, graph and front-door estimand family with latent common cause U for one declared graph; complete printed DoWhy output is regenerated without numerical estimation.
independence_basis: Repository-authored public black-box CausalModel.identify_effect calls import no Antecedent implementation or test helpers. Inputs are the declared graph and explicit observed variable names. Two dummy rows provide a schema only; no data values enter graph identification. Product assertions require an estimand expression rather than the always-present method heading.
historical_exposure: Original generation environment and harness were deleted; historical author exposure cannot be established. Current review inspected product assertions and official DoWhy public API documentation. No upstream implementation or test source was consulted or copied.
redistribution: Only repository-authored harness, frozen graph/output and dependency lock are retained under MIT OR Apache-2.0. DoWhy and transitive packages remain isolated tooling; their sources/tests are not copied into the product or ordinary CI.
limitations: A single small graph does not establish completeness, all ADMG structures, positivity, effect estimation, uncertainty, weighted/missing-data handling or calibration. Front-door identification status is distinct from the separate product enumerated-SCM intervention-value assertion. Exact rendering is pinned by the full lock; other environments need a reviewed comparison rather than silently accepting changed output. Product-side DOT preparation uses the repository latent projection; the independent DoWhy call does not. The current simple latent-common-cause projection is exercised by oracle_dot unit assertions; no general projection-correctness review is claimed.
